words.childMeaning: A long vehicle that travels on metal tracks.
practiceSentences: The train has many long carriages.
When does the train arrive?
Theo, I can see the train!
I wave at the passing train.
A train carries people to another town.

words.childMeaning: A snail is a small animal that carries a shell on its back.
practiceSentences: Nora found a snail on the wet garden path.
The snail moved slowly across the leaf.
A snail carries its shell wherever it goes.
Leo watched a snail climb the flower pot.
The snail hid inside its shell when it rained.

words.childMeaning: The part at the back of an animal's body that can move.
practiceSentences: The cat curled its tail around its paws.
Amal drew a long tail on her paper fish.
A monkey can hang from a branch by its tail.
The puppy wagged its tail when Leo came home.
That bird has bright feathers in its tail.

words.childMeaning: To sail means to travel on water in a boat.
practiceSentences: We will sail across the lake in a small boat.
The little boat can sail when the wind blows.
Amal watched the ships sail out to sea.
Grandpa taught Leo how to sail.
They sail to the island every summer.

words.childMeaning: To stay in one place until something happens.
practiceSentences: She could not wait for the next partner activity at school.
She could not wait for Saturday, when a brand new school week would begin.
"Wait," she said kindly.
Amal and her classmates could hardly wait.
She could not wait for morning, so she could watch them again.

words.childMeaning: A group of seven days that follow one after another.
practiceSentences: Amal learned something new on every day of her first week.
How many days are there in one week?
“You had a wonderful first week,” said Amal's mother.
I visit my grandmother once a week.
A new week starts again after Friday.

words.childMeaning: One of the twelve parts of a year.
practiceSentences: February is the shortest month of the year.
In which month were you born?
“My birthday is in the month of June,” said Leo.
I count the days until my favourite month.
Each month has its own page on the calendar.

words.childMeaning: A year is twelve months, from January to December.
practiceSentences: There are twelve months in one year.
Leo grew taller this year.
We plant new seeds every year.
Last year Amal learned to ride a bike.
The new year starts in January.

words.childMeaning: Again means one more time, after doing it before.
practiceSentences: Birds began to visit again.
“Let me try again,” said Leo.
Amal read her old work again.
The sun was low again, and Amal's shadow grew long.
She shook the red rug outside so that it was clean again.

words.childMeaning: Next means the thing that comes right after this one.
practiceSentences: What happens next in the story?
Leo sat next to his best friend.
Nora, you go next!
The next page showed a picture of a lion.
Nora put up her hand next.

words.childMeaning: Then means next, or after that.
practiceSentences: Then came the surprise.
Then came two small leaves.
“Then we are a team,” she said.
Then Amal made her new booklet.
Then Leo passed the stick to Amal.

words.childMeaning: An aunt is the sister of your mother or father, or your uncle's wife.
practiceSentences: My aunt gave me a new pencil.
Does your aunt live near the river?
Look, Nora's aunt is planting a tree!
Our aunt helps us pick up litter.
"I can see three small brown birds in that bush," whispers his aunt.

words.childMeaning: People means more than one person.
practiceSentences: He kept the people safe.
Come and meet the people in my neighbourhood.
People were buying fish, fruit and bright cloth.
“People cut them down for wood,” she said softly.
Many people were waiting at the bus stop.

words.childMeaning: About means on the subject of something, or roughly.
practiceSentences: What is this book about?
Leo told his friend about his word hunt.
Tell me about your favourite animal!
There are about ten children in the group.
Listen to this story about Maya and her new partner, Nora.

words.childMeaning: Around means on every side of something, or turning to look in every direction.
practiceSentences: Maya turned around to see who was calling her.
Can you look around and find your pencil?
Nora walked around the garden twice.
There were books scattered around the room.
Maya looked around the room.

words.childMeaning: Each means every one, taken one at a time.
practiceSentences: Each runner passes a stick to the next one.
She loved her street because everyone helped each other.
She liked how they helped each other, just like a big family.
Read the poem and do each action as you say it: Reach for the sky!
Amal gave each friend a paper star.

words.childMeaning: Every means each one, with none left out.
practiceSentences: Every child in the class had a partner.
Did you read every page of the book?
Every morning, Amal walks to school with Nora.
We say hello to every visitor.
And every time we read a word, we learn something new.

words.childMeaning: If tells you what happens when something else is true.
practiceSentences: If it rains, we will stay inside.
Ask Teacher Yasmin if you need help.
If you are kind, you will make friends.
Leo will come if his mum says yes.
We can go to the park if the sun shines.

words.childMeaning: A space inside a house with walls, a floor and a door.
practiceSentences: My room is small and tidy.
Which room is yours, Adam?
What a bright room this is!
Grandma sits in the front room.
We eat together in this room.

words.childMeaning: An opening in a wall with glass that lets light in.
practiceSentences: Idris looked through the window at the big tree.
Is your window open or closed tonight?
“Look outside the window!” called Father.
I can see the market from my bedroom window.
The window above the sofa lets in the morning sun.

words.childMeaning: A piece of furniture with a flat top and legs.
practiceSentences: Idris wiped the little table until the dust was gone.
Is the lamp on the table or on the shelf?
“Put the plates on the table, please,” said Mother.
I do my homework at the kitchen table.
The table stands between two wooden chairs.

words.childMeaning: A table where you sit to read and write at school.
practiceSentences: My desk is by the window.
Is this your desk, Adam?
What a tidy desk that is!
Amal puts her book on the desk.
We share one desk in our class.

words.childMeaning: One of the seven parts of a week.
practiceSentences: Every school day begins with the register.
Which day of the week do you like best?
“Today is a busy day,” said Amal's mother.
I read for ten minutes every day.
The day after Wednesday is Thursday.

words.childMeaning: To stay means to keep still, or to remain in one place.
practiceSentences: Stay calm and do not wave your arms.
Amal will stay at her grandma's house tonight.
Please stay behind the yellow line.
The puppy learned to sit and stay.
We stay inside when the rain is heavy.

words.childMeaning: A flat container used for carrying or holding things.
practiceSentences: Leo carried his lunch on a blue tray.
Put the wet paint pots on the tray.
Nora filled a tray with small seeds.
The tray was too heavy for one person.
Grandma brought the tea in on a tray.

words.childMeaning: A key is a small metal thing that opens a lock.
practiceSentences: Mum turned the key in the front door.
Leo lost the key to his bicycle lock.
The key hangs on a hook in the kitchen.
Amal found a tiny key under the mat.
You need a key to open this gate.

words.childMeaning: To need something means you must have it.
practiceSentences: I need to find the hospital.
Plants need water and light to grow.
You need a coat when it is cold.
We need three more chairs for the table.
Leo said he did not need any help.

words.childMeaning: A person who grows food and looks after farm animals.
practiceSentences: The farmer fills the water trough before the sun gets hot.
How early does the farmer wake up to milk the cows?
“Mind the wet path,” the farmer said as we walked into the field.
I helped a farmer pick beans at my uncle's farm last year.
Every market day the farmer brings fresh vegetables into town.

words.childMeaning: A person who helps people who are ill and makes them better.
practiceSentences: Doctor Sarah works at the clinic beside the post office.
When did the doctor last check your ears, Maya?
“Open wide and say ah,” said the doctor with a smile.
My little brother Idris was not afraid of the doctor at all.
The doctor wrote a note so that I could rest at home for two days.

words.childMeaning: A person who cares for people who are ill or hurt.
practiceSentences: The nurse weighed the baby and wrote the number in a small blue book.
How many hours does a nurse work in one long night?
“You were very brave today,” the nurse told Mina.
I want to thank the nurse who looked after my grandmother.
At the school clinic a nurse checks our eyes every year.

words.childMeaning: A person who drives a car, a bus or a lorry.
practiceSentences: The bus driver, Nadia, waved.
The driver stopped so the children could cross.
Every driver must watch the road carefully.
Amal thanked the driver as she got off.
The lorry driver brought boxes to the shop.

words.childMeaning: The police are people whose job is to keep everyone safe.
practiceSentences: A police officer named Rami arrived on his bicycle.
The police help people who are lost.
We called the police when the dog ran away.
A police car has a bright blue light.
The police station is next to the library.

words.childMeaning: To shout, or to phone someone to ask for help.
practiceSentences: If there is a fire, you must call for help.
Did you call the doctor about your sore throat?
Amal, call your mum and tell her the good news!
The children call Leila whenever they visit the fire station.
I will call you when the food is ready.

words.childMeaning: Buy means to get something by paying money for it.
practiceSentences: Did you buy any bread at the shop?
Leo went to buy bread with his mother.
Can we buy some apples, please?
Sami saved his money to buy a book.
After breakfast, Leo walked to the market with his mother to buy bread.

words.childMeaning: Work means the tasks or jobs that people do.
practiceSentences: Leo's father goes to work every morning.
Is this your best work, Maya?
Well done, that is great work!
The class began their partner work quietly.
"Many good people work here," he said.

words.childMeaning: Both means the two of them together.
practiceSentences: Grandma Hana hugged them both.
Both girls finished the race.
Amal and Leo both like reading.
Hold the tray with both hands.
Both windows were open in the warm room.

words.childMeaning: Many means a large number of people or things.
practiceSentences: How many books are on the shelf?
There were many children at the party.
So many stars are out tonight!
Nora has many friends at school.
How many chairs do we need for the visitors?

words.childMeaning: More means a larger number or amount.
practiceSentences: “Tomorrow, let's look for even more.”
“I can read, write and speak more clearly now,” she wrote.
There are more kinds of insects than any other animal.
We need more chairs for the visitors.
Leo wanted more time to finish.

words.childMeaning: Most means nearly all of them, or the largest amount.
practiceSentences: Which page are you most proud of, Amal?
Most of the class chose the blue paper.
This is the most useful book on the shelf.
Most birds build a nest in spring.
Nora ate most of her lunch.

words.childMeaning: Other means the second one, or the ones that are left.
practiceSentences: The other half of the apple is in the bowl.
“Put it on the shelf, next to the other books,” said Amal.
Hold the rope with your other hand.
The other children waited at the gate.
One shoe was here, but where was the other?

words.childMeaning: A child is a young person who is not grown up yet.
practiceSentences: Every child in my class can read.
Is that child your sister?
What a kind child she is!
One child sat by the window.
Each child has a name tag.

words.childMeaning: To keep means to have something and not give it away.
practiceSentences: “Keep watching,” said Adam, turning the ball further.
Fix what needs fixing, and keep the pages that are already strong.
You can keep the pencil I lent you.
Amal will keep her books in this box.
Keep your hands warm inside your gloves.

words.childMeaning: A boot is a strong shoe that covers your foot and ankle.
practiceSentences: Leo pulled on a muddy boot.
One boot was under the bed.
Amal wears a boot on each foot in the rain.
The boot was too small for Theo.
Nora shook the sand out of her boot.

words.childMeaning: Cool means a little bit cold, but not too cold.
practiceSentences: The water in the stream felt cool.
A cool wind blew across the field.
Let the soup cool before you eat it.
Amal sat in the cool shade of the tree.
The evening air was cool and fresh.

words.childMeaning: A person who makes food for other people to eat.
practiceSentences: My mum is a wonderful cook.
Who is the cook at school?
Samira, I will be the cook today!
I help the cook wash the rice.
The cook stirs the big pot.

words.childMeaning: Pull means to move something towards you.
practiceSentences: Pull the rope as hard as you can.
Amal had to pull the heavy door open.
Do not pull the cat's tail.
Leo will pull the cart up the path.
Pull your chair closer to the table.

words.childMeaning: Push means to move something away from you.
practiceSentences: Push the gate gently so it does not bang.
Nora had to push the box across the floor.
Push the button to start the machine.
Do not push in the line, please.
Leo gave the swing a little push.

words.childMeaning: To move means to go from one place to another.
practiceSentences: Today is “Get Up and Move” day at Amal's school.
Please move your bag off the chair.
The shadow will move as the sun goes down.
We watched the snail move slowly along.
Leo had to move to see the board.

words.childMeaning: To hold means to keep something in your hands.
practiceSentences: Hold this end of the rope while I pull.
Amal will hold the door for Nora.
Can you hold my book for a minute?
Leo likes to hold the baby rabbit.
Hold on tight while the bus moves.

words.childMeaning: To take means to pick something up and carry it with you.
practiceSentences: In a relay, the runners take turns.
Take one sheet and pass the rest along.
Take your coat, because it is cold.
Amal will take the letter to school.
Please take one card each.

words.childMeaning: To make an effort to do something, even if it is hard.
practiceSentences: The children got to try on Leila's helmet.
Will you try the new game with me?
Zuri, try to answer this tricky question!
Omar likes to try a new bread recipe every month.
Try it yourself tomorrow.

words.childMeaning: Sick means feeling unwell or having an illness.
practiceSentences: Leo was sick and stayed at home.
Amal felt sick after the long bus ride.
The nurse looks after children who are sick.
A sick plant has yellow leaves.
Tell an adult if you feel sick.

words.childMeaning: Having lots of power in your body or your muscles.
practiceSentences: Adam is strong enough to carry two heavy bags.
Which animal do you think is the strongest?
“Stand tall and make your legs feel strong,” said Teacher Yasmin.
I feel strong after I climb the ladder at the park.
Strong bones grow when we eat well and move often.

words.childMeaning: To finish means to come to the end of something.
practiceSentences: Leo will finish his drawing after lunch.
Did you finish the whole book?
Amal was the first to finish the race.
We must finish before the bell rings.
Finish your milk and then we can go.

words.childMeaning: Learn means to find out how to do something new.
practiceSentences: Amal wants to learn a new word each day.
Amal wants to learn how to swim.
We learn a new spelling pattern each week.
Leo will learn the song by Friday.
You learn more when you ask questions.

words.childMeaning: Along means moving forward together with something, or beside it.
practiceSentences: Sing along with the rest of the class.
Zuri walked along the river to her burrow.
Will you come along with us?
The children hurried along!
Walk along the wall until you reach the gate.

words.childMeaning: Across means from one side of something to the other side.
practiceSentences: Can you hop across the playground?
Nora ran across the grass to catch up.
Look across the field, Theo!
We walked across the bridge to the park.
The children hopped on one foot across the field.

words.childMeaning: Through means moving from one side of something to the other.
practiceSentences: Sami ran through the park.
Can you see through the window?
What an adventure, walking through the tunnel!
The children went through the gate together.
The octopus moved its eight arms slowly through the water.

words.childMeaning: As can mean at the same time, or in the same way.
practiceSentences: “I am running as fast as I can,” Amal puffed.
Amal sang as she walked to school.
It was just as Adam had said.
She found her garden promise as well.
“Our second job is just as important,” said Leila.

words.childMeaning: Than is used when you compare two things.
practiceSentences: “Helping him was better than the market,” she said.
One morning Amal laughed and said my shadow was taller than me.
Your ears will find the missing full stops faster than your eyes will.
There are more kinds of insects in the world than any other type of animal.
This box is heavier than that one.

words.childMeaning: Catch means to grab hold of something moving through the air.
practiceSentences: Zuri ran to catch the falling leaf.
Can you catch the bus at nine o'clock?
Adam tried to catch the butterfly gently.
Dogs love to catch a ball in the park.
Kiki jumped up to catch the mango before it fell.

words.childMeaning: To hit your two hands together to make a sound.
practiceSentences: Mina claps loudly when her friend finishes the race.
Can you clap in time with the drum?
“Clap twice if you can hear me,” said Teacher Yasmin.
I clap my hands to keep the beat while we sing.
The whole class claps for every runner on sports day.

words.childMeaning: Kick means to hit something with your foot.
practiceSentences: Adam can kick the ball very far.
Can you kick it to me?
What a strong kick that was!
Amal kicked the ball to Adam.
We kick the ball at break time.

words.childMeaning: To make a happy sound when something is funny.
practiceSentences: The children laugh at the puppy.
Why did you laugh?
I laugh because it is funny!
I laugh with my little sister.
We all laugh together at dinner.

words.childMeaning: Ride means to travel on or in something, like a vehicle.
practiceSentences: Amal would love to ride on the fire engine.
Can you ride a bicycle to school?
What fun it is to ride so fast!
Leila and her team ride to every fire quickly.
Theo learned to ride a horse at the farm.

words.childMeaning: To rest with your eyes closed, usually at night.
practiceSentences: Babies sleep for most of the day.
What time do you sleep on a school night?
“A good sleep helps you learn,” said Doctor Sarah.
I sleep for ten hours and wake up full of energy.
Cats sleep in the sunny corner of the room.

words.childMeaning: A smile is the happy shape your mouth makes when you are pleased.
practiceSentences: Adam had a smile on his face.
Can you give me a smile, Amal?
What a lovely smile, Amal!
Her smile made everyone feel happy.
Amal smiled a big smile.

words.childMeaning: To be up on your feet, and not sitting down.
practiceSentences: Leo stands beside the door and waits for his class.
How long can you stand on one foot?
“Stand tall and take a deep breath,” said Teacher Yasmin.
I stand up when my grandmother Hana comes into the room.
The runners stand in a line before the race begins.

words.childMeaning: A throw is when a player sends something like a ball through the air.
practiceSentences: In the throw, the elephant sent the ball flying far.
How far can you throw a ball?
Nice throw, Theo!
Amal practised her throw before the race.
Zuri can throw the ball right across the field.

words.childMeaning: A page is one side of a sheet of paper in a book.
practiceSentences: Amal turned to the next page.
Which page are we on, Adam?
What a colourful page this is!
Read the first page out loud.
My favourite page has a picture of a cat.

words.childMeaning: Letters put together that mean something when we read them.
practiceSentences: Amal found a new word on the cereal box.
Which word on this page is the longest?
“Say the word slowly,” said Teacher Yasmin.
I add one new word to my word book every day.
Words are all around us, even on our shoes.

words.childMeaning: A letter is one of the signs we use to write words, like a or b.
practiceSentences: The first letter of my name is A.
Which letter comes after b?
That letter is hard to write!
Amal traced the letter with her finger.
Every word is made of letters.

words.childMeaning: A drawing, a painting or a photo of something.
practiceSentences: Nora's picture shows a green tree and a blue sky.
Can you describe the picture on this page?
“Draw a picture for your poem,” said Teacher Yasmin.
I put my picture on the classroom wall.
Every picture in this book helps us guess the words.

words.childMeaning: A flat tool with marks on it for measuring and drawing straight lines.
practiceSentences: Leo keeps his ruler flat inside his pencil case.
Where did you put the long wooden ruler?
“Hold the ruler still,” said Nora, pointing at the mark.
My ruler shows thirty centimetres from one end to the other.
A ruler gives the same answer for everybody in the class.

words.childMeaning: A board is a flat surface on the wall that the teacher writes on.
practiceSentences: The teacher wrote our names on the board.
Can you see the board, Adam?
What a big board that is!
Amal points to a word on the board.
We copy the letters from the board.

words.group: Spelling: igh says the long i
words.childMeaning: The brightness that lets us see things.
practiceSentences: The morning light came through the kitchen window.
How much light do you need to read your book?
“Turn on the lamp, please. We need more light,” said Hana.
I like the soft light in the evening.
Without light we cannot see any colours.

words.group: Spelling: igh says the long i
words.childMeaning: Giving out or sending back a lot of light.
practiceSentences: The midday sun is so bright that I close my eyes.
Which star looks brightest tonight?
“What a bright morning!” said Nora.
I wore a hat because the sunshine was bright.
A bright lamp helps me read in the evening.

words.group: Spelling: igh says the long i
words.childMeaning: Far above the ground or above another level.
practiceSentences: The sun is high above the school at midday.
How high can a kite fly in the sky?
“The moon is high tonight,” said Grandma Hana.
I watched a bird fly high over the roof.
When the sun is high, our shadows are short.

words.group: Spelling: igh says the long i
words.childMeaning: Sight is what you can see, or the power to see.
practiceSentences: The rainbow was a lovely sight.
We use our sight to read words.
The ship was still in sight.
Grandpa's sight is not as sharp as it was.
The birds flew out of sight.

words.childMeaning: The invisible gases all around us that we breathe in.
practiceSentences: After the rain, the air smelled fresh and clean.
Why does the air feel cooler under a big tree?
“Take a deep breath of this air,” said Nora.
I love the air near the river in the morning.
Smoke from burning rubbish makes the air dirty.

words.childMeaning: A fire is something burning, with flames and heat.
practiceSentences: “They are putting out the fire,” said her mother.
Teacher Yasmin's class visited the fire station on a sunny Tuesday morning.
Never play near a fire.
The fire kept the room warm.
Grandpa lit a small fire to cook the food.

words.childMeaning: During means all through the time that something happens.
practiceSentences: We stay inside during a storm.
The room stays quiet during the test.
Do not talk during the test.
The birds sing during the early morning.
Amal took notes during the lesson.

words.childMeaning: Until means up to the time when something happens.
practiceSentences: Zuri waited until the bell rang.
Will you stay until the story ends?
Leo counted until he reached one hundred.
Wait here until I come back!
Nora read until it was time for dinner.

words.childMeaning: Once means one time, or at a time in the past.
practiceSentences: It hopped once, then settled into the grass and began to chirp again.
Along the bank, where tall trees once grew, the land was empty and brown.
We visit Grandma once a week.
Amal has been to the sea once.
Read the poem once more, please.

words.childMeaning: Already means before now, or sooner than expected.
practiceSentences: Amal liked him already, on the first day.
Have you already finished your reading?
Leo was already waiting by the gate.
It is already time for lunch!
She liked him already.

words.childMeaning: Almost means very nearly, but not quite.
practiceSentences: I look down at my feet, and my shadow has almost disappeared.
It was almost dry.
Leo almost finished the whole book.
It is almost time for lunch.
The jug is almost full of water.

words.childMeaning: A tiny point of light in the night sky. The sun is a star.
practiceSentences: Amal counted fifty stars and then gave up.
How many stars can you see tonight?
“Each star is a sun far away,” said Grandma Hana.
I like watching the stars from our doorstep.
The stars come out when the sky grows dark.

words.childMeaning: Bring means to take something with you to a place.
practiceSentences: Please bring your book to school.
Can you bring me a cup, Adam?
Bring your picture to the front!
Amal will bring her mat tomorrow.
We bring fruit for break time.

words.childMeaning: Carry means to hold something and move it with you.
practiceSentences: Amal helps carry the shopping.
Can you carry this bag, Adam?
Carry it with two hands!
Grandma carries water from the well.
The men carry the heavy box.

words.childMeaning: A colour is what we see, like red, blue or green.
practiceSentences: My favourite colour is blue.
What colour is your bag, Adam?
What a bright colour that is!
Amal will colour the sky blue.
The flag has three colours.

words.childMeaning: Count means to say numbers in order to find how many.
practiceSentences: "Let us count the grapes," said Grandpa.
Can you count to ten, Adam?
Count the hens in the yard!
Amal counts her pencils every day.
We count together in class.

words.childMeaning: To cut means to use something sharp to make things shorter or in pieces.
practiceSentences: Adam helped cut some paper for the poster.
Why did they cut down that old tree?
Careful, Amal, that pair of scissors can cut!
Fewer trees are cut down when we recycle.
Omar used a knife to cut the bread into slices.

words.childMeaning: Open means to move something so you can go in or see inside.
practiceSentences: Please open the door, Adam.
Can you open this tin, Mum?
Open your book at page one!
Amal opened the window slowly.
The shop is open every morning.

words.childMeaning: To write means to put words or letters onto paper using a pen or pencil.
practiceSentences: Sami's mother asked him to write it down.
Can you write the date on your page?
Write your ideas here, Nora!
I will write a letter to my aunt.
Amal wants to write a poem for her grandma.

words.childMeaning: Little in size; it does not take up much space.
practiceSentences: Maya carried the small basket to the reading corner.
Can a small stone be heavier than a big leaf?
“My hands are too small for this jar,” said Leo.
I keep my small coins inside a round tin box.
The small window lets in only a little light.

words.childMeaning: High from the bottom to the top, like a tree or a person.
practiceSentences: Theo stood up straight to show how tall he is.
How tall are you in centimetres this year?
“Being tall does not mean you go first,” said Amal.
I want to be as tall as my big brother.
The tall shelf holds all of our reading books.

words.childMeaning: Young means not having lived very long.
practiceSentences: The young chick follows the hen.
Is your sister young, Adam?
What a young puppy that is!
Amal is younger than her brother.
Young plants need water every day.

words.childMeaning: The colour you get when you mix red and blue.
practiceSentences: The purple flowers grow beside our gate.
Is your favourite colour purple?
“I painted my door purple,” said Maya.
I keep my purple crayon in my pencil case.
Purple grapes taste sweet in the summer.

words.childMeaning: Having a colour between black and white.
practiceSentences: The sky turned grey before the rain came.
Is the sky grey or blue today?
“Those grey clouds look heavy,” said Adam.
I wore my coat under the grey sky.
Grey clouds hide the sun and take away our shadows.

words.childMeaning: A round shape with no corners and no straight sides.
practiceSentences: The clock face on our classroom wall is a circle.
Can you draw a circle without lifting your pencil?
“Sit in a circle for story time,” said Teacher Yasmin.
